$comment: The Program EQ's parameters, declared once.
Both the C++ dispatch and the TypeScript control table are generated from
this file. See motionwave/manifests/fx-01-motion-shaper.json for why: a
parity check between two hand-maintained tables is a test that passes for a
long time and then fails once, after the drift has shipped.
Most `apply` bodies read the network's settings back and write one field.
That is not indirection for its own sake — dyn-01 §3.10 records that one
selector is shared by two legs on each band, so the eight EQ controls are
one network with eight ways in, and a dispatch that kept its own copy of
them would be a second opinion about the network's state.

params.name: Low Frequency
params.note: One selector for both low legs, which is precisely why they interact rather than cancelling.

params.name: Low Boost
Low Atten
High Frequency
High Boost
Bandwidth
params.note: Sets the Q of the high boost bell and nothing else, which test 7 asserts to within a tenth of a decibel.

params.name: Atten Select
High Atten
EQ In
params.note: Removes the passive network only. The amplifier and both transformers stay in circuit, which is what test 2 measures from two directions.

params.name: Variance
params.note: One scalar for every per-instance deviation. Two engineering trims would make a user calibrate a plug-in, and on the hardware the deviations are correlated anyway.

params.name: Oversampling
Noise
params.note: Scales the manual's own figure rather than naming a level: at 1 the floor is 92 dB below +10 dBm, which is what the hardware specifies, and at 0 it is off for anyone measuring. Its render-delta gate is -110 dBFS rather than the suite's -70 for the obvious reason: the parameter's whole job is to sit at -104 dBFS, so a gate above that would grade a working control as a dead one.
